name: Revolut USD Stablecoin
oneLiner: RUSD is Revolut's pre-launch USD stablecoin proposal under MiCA rails (CySEC CASP + Lithuanian EMI); ticker, chains, and reserve disclosures still unannounced.
collateral: Planned 1:1 USD-equivalent reserves held by Revolut's Lithuanian EMI under MiCA Title IV (EMT) safeguarding rules; exact composition (cash, MMF, segregated bank accounts) unannounced.
pegMechanism: Planned MiCA-compliant electronic-money token issued by Revolut's Lithuanian EMI with 1:1 USD mint and redemption; distribution and chain selection unannounced.

jurisdiction.regulator: CySEC (MiCA CASP) and Bank of Lithuania (EMI)

launchPhaseDetail: Companion to the already-tracked RGBP (Revolut GBP). Revolut secured a MiCA CASP licence from Cyprus (CySEC) on Oct 23 2025 and operates an existing EMI licence in Lithuania — the legal foundations for issuing e-money tokens under MiCA Title IV. In October 2025, Revolut launched fee-free 1:1 USD↔stablecoin swaps (USDC/USDT on Ethereum, Solana, and Tron) for its 65M users; stablecoin payment volumes on the platform surged 156% in 2025 to ~$10.5B. In February 2026, the FCA selected Revolut as one of 4 firms (from 20 applicants) for a UK stablecoin payment testing pilot — though that sandbox is specifically for a GBP token, not USD. Revolut received a full UK banking licence from the PRA (Mar 11 2026) and filed an OCC national bank charter application for Revolut Bank US, N.A. (Mar 5 2026, targeting a 2027 US launch with built-in stablecoin access). A Revolut-branded proprietary USD stablecoin has not been officially confirmed; the USD path runs through the Lithuanian EMI / MiCA EMT route, and Polymarket currently puts the probability at ~33% by year-end 2026. Specific ticker, chain selection, and reserve disclosure model remain unannounced.

featuredContent.title: Revolut secures MiCA license in Cyprus, expanding regulated crypto services across Europe
featuredContent.description: CySEC MiCA authorisation lets Revolut passport regulated crypto services across the 30 EEA countries; 65M global users; Crypto 2.0 platform unveiled alongside.

featuredContent.title: Revolut secures MiCA license in Cyprus, is a stablecoin next?
featuredContent.description: EU counsel describes a Revolut stablecoin in 2026 as 'plausible' under MiCA; clarifies that the Cyprus CASP licence does not itself authorise issuance, which must come via Revolut's Lithuanian EMI.

featuredContent.title: Revolut Plans 2027 US Bank Launch With Stablecoin Services Built In From Day One
Revolut's US bank to offer stablecoin services alongside FDIC-insured products: Reuters
featuredContent.description: Reuters reports Revolut's planned US national bank will integrate stablecoin services with FDIC-insured accounts from launch; own-issuance of a Revolut USD token remains unconfirmed.

milestones.title: Revolut Digital Assets Europe receives MiCA CASP licence from CySEC
milestones.description: Revolut's Cyprus entity gets MiCA authorisation to passport regulated crypto services across the EEA; unveils 'Crypto 2.0' platform with 1:1 stablecoin/USD conversion as a flagship feature.

milestones.title: EU counsel describes a Revolut USD/EUR stablecoin in 2026 as 'plausible' under MiCA
milestones.description: Decrypt reports Revolut's Lithuanian EMI provides the EMT issuer foundation; Cyprus CASP licence is the service-provider side; sources say Revolut has been working on its own stablecoin for over a year.

milestones.title: FCA selects Revolut for UK stablecoin payment testing pilot
milestones.description: Revolut is one of 4 firms chosen from 20 applicants to trial stablecoin products in real-world UK conditions from Q1 2026; use cases include stablecoin payments, wholesale settlement, and crypto trading. Results will inform the FCA's crypto regulatory framework targeting October 2027.

milestones.title: Revolut files OCC national bank charter application (Revolut Bank US, N.A.)
milestones.description: Revolut applies for a US national bank charter with a $500M investment commitment, targeting a 2027 US bank launch with built-in stablecoin access (third-party USDC/USDT, not confirmed own issuance).

milestones.title: Revolut receives full UK banking licence from the PRA
milestones.description: Revolut exits mobilisation; 13M UK customers gain FSCS protection. A GBP stablecoin would be issued from Revolut's e-money entity, not the UK bank.

milestones.title: Revolut confirms its planned US national bank will offer stablecoin services alongside FDIC-insured accounts
milestones.description: Reuters reports Revolut Bank US, N.A. (OCC charter applicant) will offer stablecoin services alongside FDIC-insured products from day one, though own-issuance of a Revolut USD token remains unconfirmed; the USD path continues to run through the Lithuanian EMI / MiCA EMT route.
